title: London, Sunny
subtitle: And so, they set off on a new adventure.

trails.title: Daily Newspaper Excerpts
trails.description: A collection of clippings compiled by an avid Daily Inquirer reader and diehard Uluru Games fan.

content.text: Post-Qualifiers Prospects: Setting Out Beneath Clear Skies

Following the Uluru London Qualifiers, 32 athletes from Britain, competing in 18 different events, departed for Australia aboard an Imperial Airways flight this morning. The weather was exceptionally clear with fresh air and no visible smog. Imperial Airways personnel commented that it was "an exceedingly rare occurrence, an ideal omen for their momentous journey."

    Reports suggest that the rare clear skies may be related to the "Fog Monster Incident" during the qualifiers. Many claim that Willow's floor ritual routine banished both the fog and the phantom beast, while skeptics argue that the Witch staged the entire event, using a sinister spectacle to manipulate public sentiment. Others have even claimed to hold insider knowledge indicating this to be part of a century-long conspiracy orchestrated by the British government ...

    Whatever the truth of the matter, the Uluru qualifiers have brought tangible benefits to London. Hospital admissions for respiratory conditions have dropped by 60%, with many residents reporting easier breathing and air quality "reminiscent of centuries past."

items.text: One week later.
*knock-knock*

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: Come in.
Foundation Office
A figure in brown enters the Foundation office. By the window, Madam Z turns to face her.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Madam Z, here's the report for my mission.
Tooth Fairy sets a thick report down at the corner of the desk.
Madam Z's desk is cluttered with papers.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It seems you've been busy too.
Madam Z winces a little as she takes a sip from her mug. The strength of her tea seems to correspond with her increasing workload. As the stack of documents grows, the more bitter it becomes.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: Even though we've confirmed the connection between societal turbulence and the "Storm," there is no time to catch a breath.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: Once chaos breaks, it will be the end of another era, but we can't resist the inevitable. All we can do is maintain order to postpone it as long as possible.
Madam Z heaves a soft sigh as the steam from her mug swirls unnaturally.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: So, any findings in London?
Tooth Fairy opens her hand flat. There's a speck of coal dust and a baby tooth resting in it.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: A Walpurgis's tooth, from the black fog, and the last baby tooth of a child. Very rare, even for my collection.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: Hmm.
Madam Z pushes her glasses up and holds her breath as she inches forward.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: Right. Well, that's good to know.
After a few moments of examination, she straightens her posture.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: I heard the London branch is still trying to replicate the ritual that was carried out at the Exhibition Games. What was that?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It was a coincidence, actually.
Tooth Fairy peers out the window, watching the soft, white clouds gathered on the horizon. Perhaps London, too, is enjoying such beautiful weather.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: After analyzing the live sample provided by Mr. Fog, the London branch concluded that the Walpurgis is a mutant of the Cyoeraeth, a critter species that's been extinct for centuries.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Ms. Willow lent one of her heirlooms to the London branch after the Games, a book that details an ancient ritual meant to worship the god of the sun. This is the ritual she performed on the floor.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: But when Ms. Willow performed the ritual again in front of the Walpurgis, nothing happened.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: My guess is that, since the Cyoeraeth disappeared, the ritual fell out of use and became fragmented over the years. Her version of it is probably incomplete.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: The conditions must've happened to align at that moment to allow the ritual to work. It could've been any combination of things—Ms. Willow's dancing, the music from the didgeriwood, the fire from the torch, the magnetic fields around the stadium ...

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Or perhaps it was all of them. The ritual also happened to have the power to capture the Walpurgis, which put an end to the heavy smog in London.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It makes sense, really, that a ritual used to worship the god of the sun would capture a monster that covers the sky and plunges everyone into darkness.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: In conclusion, the ritual's success was a near-unrepeatable coincidence.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: An endangered critter and a long-forgotten ritual ...

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: I guess that's why humans are always sifting through their past. There's always wisdom to be found in history.
Madam Z takes a small sip of the tea in her mug.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: It's gone bitter. I should've finished it earlier.
She sets the mug aside and sits down at her desk.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: By the way, I've approved your vacation request.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: No one should disturb you this time.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Thank you. Have a good day.
Tooth Fairy sets another piece of milk candy on the desk and walks out.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: Milk candy ... Makes me miss the rabbit candy back home.

items.speaker: Madam Z
items.text: Well, at least it goes with the tea.
Madam Z unwraps the candy and pops it into her mouth.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow! I got it!
Flutterpage's voice arrives before she does.
Willow raises her eyes from her packing list as she hears bright little footsteps heading closer.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Look! The Foundation's recognized our Games! Here's your invitation and our tickets!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Heh. I suppose your flying does come in handy after all.
Willow shuts her suitcase and takes the folder from Flutterpage.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Are you done packin'?
Flutterpage looks around Willow's room, making note of what's moved and what hasn't.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ain't you takin' this medal with you?
Flutterpage points to the medal recently placed in the cabinet—the first Willow has earned in almost a decade.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: No. This is proof enough.
Willow pats the folder holding the invitation and two tickets.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But that medal's for the winner of the qualifiers!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, please, they're just qualifiers.
Willow scoffs.
*ding-dong*

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Who's that, I wonder?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Wow, what happened to the garden? It's beautiful!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Ms. Willow's put a lot of care into it ever since she won first place in the qualifiers.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Ah, Charlotte, ever predictable.
Caroline and Brimley look around the garden, enjoying the rare sight of foliage flourishing in winter.

items.speaker: Voiced Flower
items.text: What are you doing here?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: We want to invite you to join us. Let's go to Australia together!

items.speaker: Voiced Flower
items.text: With Caroline, too?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: For your information, Charlotte, the top three athletes all qualify for the finals. And besides, I might have beaten you if you weren't so lucky as to capture that Walpurgis.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: By the way, the ship we're taking is owned by the Bartley family.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: So, Ms. Bartley said she'd arrange a presidential suite for us.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: A presidential suite? Like, for presidents?
Flutterpage's head sticks out from behind Willow.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: It seems we'll be spending quite some time together in the coming weeks.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But which one of us is a president? It's Caroline, ain't it? It must be!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Would you shut your mouth?!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hah. You can't scare me anymore.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Heh-heh.
Dusk paints the world gold, and from a distant riverbank, a freighter sounds its horn.
Today, the skies of London are clear.
